title: Adaptive telemetry-driven retry contracts, id-key signaling, and lossy-stream handling
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and implement an adaptive, telemetry-aware retry/backoff contract across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. Introduce an explicit per-request idempotency hint field (id_key_hint) to enable safe at-most-once semantics where available, and provide SDK-first patterns for lossy or long-running streaming endpoints (e.g., token streams, file uploads). The goal is to reduce duplicate billable work, improve failure surface observability, and provide ergonomic defaults that balance correctness and user ergonomics.
acceptance_criteria: Cross-SDK API includes an optional id_key_hint parameter with standardized semantics documented in the SDK reference
Default retry profiles implemented in Python/TS/Go with deterministic mapping from error classification + telemetry bucket to backoff strategy
Streaming helper utilities in each SDK to mark a stream as 'lossy' or 'resumable' and corresponding retry behaviour defined
Telemetry hooks emit standardized metrics: retry_attempts, retry_reason, id_key_reused, stream_resume_success
Integration tests exercising client-visible duplicate suppression with id_key_hint and controlled server 5xx/connection failure injection
Documentation snippets and migration guide for existing SDK consumers
design_decisions: Expose id_key_hint as a free-form string; SDKs will canonicalize and attach a hashed id_key for transport to avoid PII
Do not mandate server-side deduplication — SDKs must expose graceful fallback when server returns duplicate-detection-not-supported
Classify errors into three categories for SDK decisions: transient-network, transient-server (retryable 5xx), and semantic/client (400-range). Only first two are candidates for automatic retries
Introduce telemetry buckets (low-latency, cold-cache, high-cost) to bias backoff and token-budget-aware retry budgets
Default profile: optimistic small-backoff for idempotent-safe requests, conservative exponential backoff for non-id-key requests, and aggressive capped fast-retries for resumed streams
implementation_notes: SDKs will ship a new RetryPolicy interface with a DefaultTelemetryPolicy implementation that consults an injected Telemetry client
Python/TS/Go will share a canonical table (in prose) mapping HTTP codes + connection errors to RetryAction (retry, no-retry, resume-if-possible)
When id_key_hint is provided, SDK will attach 'X-Redwood-Id-Key' header with base64url(hash(versioned|id_key_hint)) and include id_key metadata in telemetry events
Streaming helpers: provide StreamContext.mark_lossy() and StreamContext.resume_cursor(cursor_token) patterns; server optional cursor protocol supported via headers
Add unit + integration tests that simulate partial writes and ensure SDK does not double-send large payloads unless explicitly allowed by caller
sample_snippets:
Python example:
from redwood import Client
client = Client()
resp = client.generate(prompt="hi", id_key_hint="signup-12345")
# SDK attaches hashed id key header and will only retry safely
TypeScript example:
const client = new RedwoodClient();
const resp = await client.chat.create({ input: 'status', id_key_hint: 'order-998' });
// default policy: small immediate retry on transient network errors, exponential otherwise
Go example:
cli := redwood.New();
resp, err := cli.CreateEmbedding(ctx, req, redwood.WithIdKeyHint("batch-202603"))
// library emits telemetry: retry_reason and id_key_reused
Streaming resumable pattern (pseudo):
1) Open stream with resume=true and optional cursor_token
2) If connection fails, SDK attempts to resume up to N times using server-provided cursor
3) If resume not supported or cursor absent and stream marked lossless, fail fast; if marked lossy, return partial with warning header

estimated_risks: If servers do not implement dedup semantics, callers could rely on id_key_hint incorrectly; mitigate with traffic shaping and explicit 'dedup_supported' response header
Adding extra headers may surface PII risks — ensure hash + truncation and legal review
Complexity in mapping telemetry buckets to concrete backoff numbers — start conservative and iterate with A/B experiments
